written: 2026-11-01, before building the dataset or training
question: Does fine-tuning rfdetr_mixed_small on SoccerTrack Challenge MOT clips improve player detection on an unseen match?

data.source: SoccerTrack Challenge 2025 public Drive folder (ScoccerChllenge2025 / Training Dataset), 6 clips 4096x1080, 25 fps, 22 MOT player boxes per frame, no ball labels
data.test_match: 117092 (night) - never used for training or checkpoint selection
data.tiles_reason: player height / tile height 0.114 vs 0.123 for production panorama tiles (median MOT box 40.9 px; panorama detections 58.6 px over 476 px tiles)
data.base_dataset: data/tracking/datasets/teamtrack_mixed copied into all splits so that ball labels are kept (MOT tiles contain unlabelled balls)

training.checkpoint: checkpoint_best_total.pth as selected by rfdetr on the validation split

metrics_on_test.clip: scripts/soccertrack_v2/evaluate_detector_mot.py on 117092 clip, tiles 3, every 25, foot-point matching (<=0.5 x GT box height); IoU is not used because box drawing convention differs between TeamTrack-trained and MOT-trained models
metrics_on_test.panorama: scripts/soccertrack_v2/detection_audit.py on our 117092 panorama, segments 1 5 9 of 600-960 s, line-landmark calibration, tiles 4 (live default) via scripts/soccertrack_v2/detection_variants.py

acceptance: panorama frames with a ball detection >= 0.8 x baseline (no ball ground truth; guard against forgetting the ball class)
after_test: no change to data split, training settings, checkpoint choice or criteria; a failed model is reported and not promoted
limits: one unseen test match (night); MOT clips and panorama come from the same camera system; promotion to production would replace the default weights and is a separate step
